newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close up as blue chips, secondaries run.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close up as blue chips, secondaries run.

text.p: A clutch of blue chips joined the rally of secondaries in the afternoon to bring the share market to a higher close, traders said.
Heavyweight Telekom ended weaker but selective key blue chips rose after days of weakness due to portfolio adjustments by funds.
"This is the most active session so far this year. Both retail and institutional players were quite aggressive," said a bank-backed brokerage dealer.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 10.13 points or 0.83 percent to 1,224.55.
The Second Board index jumped 15.01 points or 2.51 percent to 612.93.
Heavyweights Maybank, United Engineers, Proton and Rothmans rose between 20 and 80 cents. Power firm Tenaga gained 20 cents to 12.70 ringgit, helped by switching of funds out of Telekom.
"I think a lot of people look at Tenaga as 'the worst is over'. That it's the heavyweight to watch," said Simone Yeo, analyst at HSBC James Capel.
Telekom fell 30 cents to 20.30 ringgit on a mix of concerns including rumours of lower-than-forecast full-year earnings and earlier start-date of a fixed line agreement.
